title: What Is Agentic Testing? Definition and Platform | TestMu AI
description: Agentic testing is when an AI agent plans, writes, runs and repairs tests toward a goal you set. See how it differs from scripted and AI-assisted testing.

hero.h1b: AI agents that plan, run and repair tests.
hero.lede: Agentic testing is software testing where an AI agent works toward a goal you set: it plans the checks, writes the steps, runs them and repairs them when the app changes. On TestMu AI, KaneAI is the agent and every run ends in a pass or fail with screenshots and logs.

sections.head: Agents for each part of QA

items.a: Agentic testing is testing driven by an AI agent that plans, writes, runs and repairs tests toward a goal you set, then reports a pass or fail with evidence.

items.q: How is agentic testing different from AI-assisted testing?
items.a: AI-assisted tools suggest steps or locators while a person drives. In agentic testing the agent completes the loop: plan, author, run and repair.
Yes: pass or fail is checked against the acceptance criteria you wrote.

items.q: Which TestMu AI product does agentic testing?
items.a: KaneAI is the agent for web and mobile apps. Kane CLI runs the same agent from a terminal and inside coding agents.

items.q: Does agentic testing replace QA engineers?
items.a: No. Engineers set goals, review generated tests and own the release decision. The agent removes the script writing and maintenance work.
